title: Berner Oberland Hut Chain — Kandersteg to Grindelwald

bestPeriod.note: The Hohtürli approach and Sefinenfurgge can hold hard snow into July; the cable-secured Chindbetti step near Hohtürli is safest dry.

summary: A hut-to-hut week on the Via Alpina from Kandersteg over Hohtürli to Blüemlisalphütte, then on through Griesalp and Mürren to Grindelwald.
hook: This is the Berner Oberland at its most classic: a steep, cable-assisted climb from Kandersteg's Oeschinensee to the Hohtürli pass and Blüemlisalphütte, a glacier-fringed SAC hut with the Blüemlisalp icefall at the door, then a Via Alpina traverse through Griesalp and over the Sefinenfurgge to Mürren, finishing along the Eiger's north face to Grindelwald. Four valleys, one waymarked national route, and a genuinely alpine week.

snapshot.Base(s): Kandersteg to start, Grindelwald to finish, huts and villages between
snapshot.Total Distance / Terrain: approx. 75–85 km, 5,800–6,400 m combined ascent; white-red-white T3 throughout, one cable-secured step near Hohtürli
snapshot.Getting There: Fly to Zürich (ZRH), train to Spiez, change for Kandersteg (about 2h total)
snapshot.Who It Suits: Fit hut-to-hut hikers comfortable with a steep cable-assisted pass and consecutive long days

itinerary.title: Kandersteg and the Oeschinensee
itinerary.morning: Arrive Kandersteg by train from Spiez. Walk or take the gondola up to Oeschinensee, one of the most photographed alpine lakes in Switzerland, sitting at 1,578 m below the Blüemlisalp wall.
itinerary.afternoon: Circle the lake on the lower path, checking the Hohtürli route's condition board at the Berghotel before returning to Kandersteg.
itinerary.evening: Early dinner; the Hohtürli climb starts before sunrise tomorrow to beat the afternoon cloud buildup.
itinerary.dayStats: 9 km, 350 m ascent, 350 m descent. Grade T1–T2, well-graded lakeside path.

itinerary.title: Hohtürli and Blüemlisalphütte
itinerary.morning: From Oeschinensee, climb the long switchbacked path toward Hohtürli (2,778 m), steepening through the final section known locally as the Chindbetti, where fixed cable assists a short exposed rock step.
itinerary.afternoon: Cross Hohtürli and drop the short distance to Blüemlisalphütte (2,834 m), a Swiss Alpine Club hut sitting directly beside the Blüemlisalp glacier, with the Blüemlisalphorn and Morgenhorn filling the skyline.
itinerary.evening: The hut terrace looks straight onto the icefall — arrive with enough daylight to sit and watch it before dinner.
itinerary.dayStats: 13 km, 1,250 m ascent, negligible descent. Grade T3, cable-secured rock step near the pass, otherwise steady switchback trail.

itinerary.title: Descent to Griesalp via the Gamchi side
itinerary.morning: From Blüemlisalphütte, descend the glacier-carved Gamchi valley on the hut's western approach, a quieter and less-trodden line than the Kandersteg side.
itinerary.afternoon: Continue down through alp pasture to Griesalp, a small road-end hamlet in the Kiental, reachable only by postbus or on foot — no through road.
itinerary.evening: Griesalp is tiny; the single guesthouse is the only option, so confirm the booking before setting out.
itinerary.dayStats: 14 km, 100 m ascent, 1,350 m descent. Grade T3, steep scree and switchback upper section, easing to forest track lower down.

itinerary.title: Sefinenfurgge to Mürren
itinerary.morning: Climb from Griesalp on the Via Alpina Route 1 waymarking toward the Sefinenfurgge (2,612 m), a demanding pass with loose rock on both approaches and, in a heavy year, old snow into July.
itinerary.afternoon: Descend into the Sefinental, passing below the Rottal glacier's outwash, and climb the final stretch to Mürren, the car-free village terraced above the Lauterbrunnen valley.
itinerary.evening: Mürren's Eiger–Mönch–Jungfrau panorama from the village promenade is one of the best in the region — worth the walk before dinner.
itinerary.dayStats: 18 km, 950 m ascent, 850 m descent. Grade T3–T4, loose rock near the Furgge, genuinely demanding in poor visibility.

itinerary.title: Gimmelwald and down to Lauterbrunnen
itinerary.morning: An easier day after Sefinenfurgge: walk or ride the cable car down to Gimmelwald, one of the smallest and least-changed villages in the valley, then continue on foot along the valley-side path.
itinerary.afternoon: Descend to Lauterbrunnen itself, in the valley of 72 waterfalls, with time to see the Staubbach Fall directly above the village.
itinerary.evening: A valley-floor rest night; gear dries out properly for the first time since Kandersteg.
itinerary.dayStats: 11 km, 150 m ascent, 950 m descent. Grade T1–T2, well-graded path and some cable-car assistance.

itinerary.title: Wengen and the Kleine Scheidegg balcony
itinerary.morning: Train from Lauterbrunnen up to Wengen, a car-free terrace village, then continue on foot along the balcony trail toward Kleine Scheidegg, with the Eiger's north face rising directly overhead.
itinerary.afternoon: Continue on the classic Männlichen or Eigergletscher path, contouring below the face before dropping toward Grindelwald.
itinerary.evening: Grindelwald marks the end of the high walking; a proper final dinner is in order.
itinerary.dayStats: 16 km, 550 m ascent, 750 m descent. Grade T2, wide balcony trail, no exposure despite the dramatic setting.

itinerary.title: Bachalpsee and departure
itinerary.morning: A last short walk: gondola to First, then the easy path out to Bachalpsee, a glacier-fed tarn that mirrors the Wetterhorn and Schreckhorn on a calm morning.
itinerary.afternoon: Return to Grindelwald, train to Interlaken and onward toward Zürich for the flight home.
itinerary.dayStats: 8 km, 200 m ascent, 200 m descent (excluding lift-assisted sections). Grade T1, easy path throughout.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel or B&B in Kandersteg
accommodationStrategy.description: Close to the Oeschinensee gondola and the train station, useful for the pre-dawn Hohtürli start on Day 2.

accommodationStrategy.name: Blüemlisalphütte
accommodationStrategy.description: Book directly through the SAC/CAS online hut reservation portal well ahead — this is one of the most popular huts in the Berner Oberland and regularly sells out on August weekends.

accommodationStrategy.name: Gasthaus in Griesalp or Mürren
accommodationStrategy.description: Griesalp has a single small guesthouse that is the only overnight in the hamlet; Mürren has more choice but fills fast in high season, given its car-free status and Eiger-north-face views.

logistics.emergency: 112 pan-European; Switzerland's alpine and helicopter rescue is Rega, on **1414**.
logistics.weather: Afternoon storms build over the glaciated peaks from around 13:00 in summer; both Hohtürli and Sefinenfurgge should be crossed in the morning.
logistics.bookingWindows: Blüemlisalphütte runs on the SAC's online reservation system; book it as soon as dates are set, since demand consistently outstrips beds through August.

other.label: Waymarks
other.text: White-red-white blazes mark the mountain trail standard used throughout this route (Bergweg, T2–T3); the short cable-secured step below Hohtürli is the only section approaching Alpine-trail character.

other.label: Griesalp access
other.text: No through road serves Griesalp; the postbus from Kiental is the only vehicle link, useful to know if weather forces an early exit from Day 3.

other.label: Via Alpina waymarking
other.text: Route 1 signage overlays the standard Swiss trail network with its own logo; follow the white-red-white blazes as the primary reference where the two diverge.

other.label: Cash
other.text: Griesalp's guesthouse and the hut bar both prefer cash; carry Swiss francs in small notes.

proTips: Book Blüemlisalphütte before anything else on this trip — it is the hardest bed on the route to secure.
Start the Hohtürli climb by 07:00; the Chindbetti cable step is far more pleasant with cool rock and no queue.
Take the Gamchi-side descent to Griesalp rather than retracing to Kandersteg — it is the quieter, more rewarding line and avoids doubling back.
Confirm the Griesalp postbus timetable before Day 3, since it is the only backup if legs or weather demand an early exit from the valley.
Walk the Kleine Scheidegg balcony in the morning; afternoon cloud regularly hides the Eiger face by early afternoon in July and August.
Reserve the First gondola for an early Day 7 slot — Bachalpsee gets crowded by mid-morning in high season.
Eat Alpkäse at the Griesalp or Mürren guesthouse rather than waiting for Grindelwald; both sit close to working alp dairies.

packingNotes: Trekking poles, essential for the Hohtürli and Sefinenfurgge descents.
Gloves for the cable-secured Chindbetti step, even though it is short.
A warm layer for the pass crossings; both sit above 2,600 m.
Sturdy boots with real ankle support for the loose rock near Sefinenfurgge.
Cash in Swiss francs for Griesalp and hut extras.
Sun protection; the glacier-adjacent terrain at Blüemlisalphütte reflects strongly.
A light rain shell — Berner Oberland weather can turn inside an hour even on a good forecast.
whatCouldGoWrong: **Snow on the Chindbetti step early in the season.** Fallback: ask the Oeschinensee Berghotel or Kandersteg tourist office for current conditions before committing; if unsafe, delay the crossing a day and use Kandersteg's lower trails instead.
**Blüemlisalphütte fully booked.** Fallback: day-hike to Hohtürli and back to Kandersteg instead, then rejoin the itinerary at Griesalp via the Kiental postbus the next morning.
**Old snow blocks the Sefinenfurgge.** Fallback: descend from Griesalp to Reichenbach and take the train around via Interlaken to Lauterbrunnen, rejoining the route at Day 5.

**Weather closes in for the Kleine Scheidegg balcony day.** Fallback: the Wengen–Grindelwald train link runs regardless of trail conditions, letting you skip the balcony walk without losing the connection.

**Fatigue after the Hohtürli–Sefinenfurgge back-to-back.** Fallback: split Day 4 by overnighting in Griesalp an extra night and treating the Sefinenfurgge crossing as a fresh, well-rested day rather than pushing straight through.
